clue.text: It helps to explain a computer terminal having a shiny case

indicators.note: the shiny word forms a case, holding the other letters inside it

parts.note: something shiny is glossy

indicators.note: a terminal is an end, so the last letter of computer is taken

explanation.surface: A screen at a computer station with a glossy casing is said to help explain things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Computer terminal' looks like hardware, but 'terminal' takes the last letter, R, of 'computer'; A and R sit in the case GLOSSY. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of difficult words with their meanings, so it helps a reader understand a text.

clue.text: Before directions are given, almost cook the salmon

indicators.note: the cooking word comes before the directions
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to grill is to cook under direct heat
S and E are compass directions, south and east

explanation.surface: Grill the fish nearly done, and only then read the recipe instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' suggests recipe steps, but it means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilse is a young salmon returning from the sea to fresh water for the first time.

clue.text: Bird seen thus rising above quarry

indicators.note: in a down entry the rising word sits above the quarry
in a down clue rising means the word for thus is read upwards

parts.note: so means thus
quarry is hunted prey

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is seen soaring over its target.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating hawk, also called the fish hawk.

clue.text: It gives the shellback propulsion at sea

definitions.text: It gives the shellback propulsion at sea

parts.words: It gives the shellback propulsion at sea
parts.note: a shellback is slang for an old sailor, but read literally it is a creature with a shell on its back, such as a lobster, and this is the limb that helps it swim

explanation.surface: Something drives a veteran sailor along on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Shellback means an old seadog, so the clue suggests a sail or engine; read literally it is a crustacean.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmeret is one of the small abdominal limbs a crustacean uses for swimming and carrying eggs.

clue.text: Fish an old woman provided to sustain an East End artist?

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting word sits beneath the other, holding it up

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, put in Bow, a district of London's East End: RA in Bow
an old trout is slang for a disagreeable old woman

explanation.surface: An elderly lady funds a struggling painter in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the artist as RA in Bow, the East End district. 'provided' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow trout is a North American game fish with a pink stripe along its side.

clue.text: Programme that is viewed in the club

parts.note: M*A*S*H was a long-running television programme set in a field hospital
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A TV show is watched in the clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewed in the' is linking padding: the club is the definition, a golfing iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie is an old name for a golf club, roughly a modern five-iron.

clue.text: Improve publicity about soldiers

indicators.note: the publicity goes about, around the soldiers

parts.note: an ad is publicity
soldiers are men

explanation.surface: Better advertising concerning the troops is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to correct or better something, as with a text or law.

clue.text: Swineherd always in evidence at the end of the year

parts.note: a hog man looks after pigs
ay is a poetic word for always, also spelt aye

explanation.surface: The pig-keeper is always to be seen when December closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in evidence at' is linking. Hogmanay is the Scottish name for New Year's Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scots celebration of 31 December, the final night of the calendar.

clue.text: Flat secured, say, at the end of the day

parts.note: flat means level or even

indicators.note: say means the word for secured is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: secured with a knot means tied

explanation.surface: An apartment is locked up as night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, but it is the adjective, EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening.

clue.text: One member allowed to be indirect

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MP, Member of Parliament
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: A single Member of Parliament is permitted to speak in a roundabout way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied rather than stated outright, so it is conveyed in a roundabout way.

clue.text: A measure of the alliance

explanation.surface: A step taken by a group of allies.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an old unit of distance of about three miles, and also a union of states or clubs bound by agreement.

clue.text: Source of a tune Dinah arranged

indicators.note: a tune arranged is reworked, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer called Dinah reworks a song, finding its origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' is the musical sense of scoring a tune, signalling the anagram of OF A TUNE DINAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountainhead is a spring from which a stream flows, figuratively an origin.

clue.text: Group of schoolchildren run out of energy

indicators.note: the run goes out, so its letter is dropped from the group's word

parts.note: in British schools a stream is a class of pupils grouped by ability
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A class of pupils is flagging, out of energy after running about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out of energy' reads as one phrase, but 'run out' removes R from STREAM, leaving the definition 'energy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is a source of power, and figuratively vigour, as in running out of steam.

clue.text: Scattered freely, it's found be-side a minor thoroughfare

indicators.note: the founding word is placed next to the road, coming after it

parts.note: a B road is a minor road in the British numbering system
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: Seed thrown about widely lands by the side of a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like 'discovered', but it is the metalworking verb, CAST. In Britain, B roads are secondary routes below A roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed sown broadcast is flung widely by hand rather than planted in rows.

clue.text: Item of equipment to which failed artists return?

definitions.text: Item of equipment to which failed artists return?

parts.words: Item of equipment to which failed artists return?
parts.note: plays on the idiom of going back to start a failed plan again from scratch, taken literally as a draughtsman's tilted desk

explanation.surface: Artists whose work has flopped go back to a piece of studio kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughtsman's sloping desk is where designs begin, so starting over means returning to it.

clue.text: Graduate teetotaller, a celebrity in several companies

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts
TT stands for teetotal
a literary lion is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A sober graduate, a famous figure, appears in various firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'companies' suggests businesses; it is the military sense. 'in' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is an army unit made up of a number of companies.

clue.text: Insular headgear worn in the monastery?

parts.note: read backwards as a recipe, the answer is headgear, a cap, placed in SULAR, which split is in sular

explanation.surface: Islanders' hats are worn by monks.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as S-CAP-ULAR: a CAP in SULAR, which is IN SULAR, read as one word 'Insular'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapular is a sleeveless monastic garment hanging from the shoulders, part of a monk's habit.

clue.text: In an Irish county, see a black cow

indicators.note: the see word goes in the Irish county

parts.note: Galway is a county in the west of Ireland
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: Out in the west of Ireland, look at a dark-coloured cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Galloway is a hardy breed of hornless, usually black, beef cattle from south-west Scotland.

clue.text: At sea, carry the component covered by this agreement

indicators.note: the part lies under cover of the muddled letters, inside them
at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: a component is a part

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, transport the parts this contract covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' turns CARRY THE into CHARTERY, and 'covered by' puts PART inside it, between CHARTER and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A charterparty is the contract by which a shipowner hires out a vessel for cargo, an apt maritime deal.

clue.text: Strong drink provided for holy man during journey

parts.note: ST, saint
in means during
go means a journey or a turn at travelling

explanation.surface: Liquor is supplied for a saint on a pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided for' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old word for strong ale.

clue.text: Theme for most of the study

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: Most of the time goes to choosing a topic for the den.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread is a running line of argument or idea through a work.

clue.text: Litter removed in the east by, bearers

definitions.text: Litter removed in the east by, bearers

parts.words: Litter removed in the east by, bearers
parts.note: litter here is not rubbish but a curtained couch, carried away on poles by porters in Asia

explanation.surface: Rubbish is carted off by porters somewhere in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Litter suggests rubbish being cleared; it is the old carried couch, and 'removed' simply means carried off. The comma after 'by' is a speck on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A palanquin is a covered seat on poles carried on the shoulders of porters in India and the Far East.

clue.text: Key kept by discriminating relative

indicators.note: the key is kept by the other word, held inside it

parts.note: nice can mean fine or discriminating, as in a nice distinction
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A selective relation holds on to the keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Leader of 7 launching appeal in a church

indicators.note: the appeal word goes inside the church letters with A before them

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A New Year figure starts an appeal from a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is the clue numbered 7-down, whose answer begins with H; the definition is that letter's spelt-out name. 'launching' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the year-end festival in 7 is H, and the name of the letter H is spelt out in full.

clue.text: He advises on the initiation of writs during a course

indicators.note: the writs letter comes during the course, inside it

parts.note: a course of bricks is a layer

indicators.note: an initiation is a beginning, so the first letter of writs is taken

explanation.surface: A legal adviser comments on starting proceedings in the middle of a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests study, but it is a layer of bricks; the W from writs is set inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor or barrister gives legal counsel to clients.

clue.text: Bold resistance of one engaged in Paris

parts.note: de is French for of
fiancé is the French word for a man engaged to marry, and in Paris also tells the solver the of is French

explanation.surface: A betrothed person living in Paris defies convention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' covers both pieces: DE and FIANCE are both French words.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open, daring refusal to obey or yield.

clue.text: A mediocre writer, Thomas of Ercildoune?

explanation.surface: Is a poor versifier the same as a medieval Scottish poet?
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas of Ercildoune, a 13th-century Scottish seer and poet, is known as Thomas the Rhymer.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster who just strings verses together is a versifier, and the Border seer Thomas bore that title as his nickname.

clue.text: Like canine transformed into dodo

definitions.note: an adjective: resembling a canine tooth

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog is turned into an extinct bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' suggests a dog, but here it is the tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Odontoid means tooth-shaped, and a canine is a pointed tooth.
